questions.text: How did Jijabai shape Shivaji's future?
questions.text_as_printed: How did Jijabai shape Shivaji's future? (Average)

answer.value: Jijabai gave Shivaji a good education and noble values from his childhood. She narrated stories from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and the lives of great heroes, inspiring patriotism, courage, and a sense of justice in him. She also encouraged him to fight against injustice. Under Jijabai's guidance and inspiration, Shivaji grew into a brave, just, and ideal ruler.

questions.text: Who was Shaista Khan? What was the outcome of his conflict with Shivaji?
questions.text_as_printed: Who was Shaista Khan? What was the outcome of his conflict with Shivaji? (Average)

answer.value: Shaista Khan was the uncle and a leading general of the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. Aurangzeb sent him to South India to defeat Shivaji. In 1663 CE, Shivaji launched a surprise attack on Shaista Khan at Pune. During the attack, Shaista Khan's fingers were injured. As a result, he had to leave the Deccan, and Shivaji's fame increased greatly.

questions.text: Explain the cultural contributions of the Mughals.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the cultural contributions of the Mughals. (Difficult)

answer.value:
Cultural contributions of the Mughals
Mughals gave special encouragement to Persian literature.
In Akbar's court there were poets like Abul Fazal, Nizamuddin, Badauni and Tulsidas.
Abul Fazal wrote Akbar Nama and Tulsidas wrote Ramcharitmanas
He wrote in Hindi.
King Darashukoh translated the Bhagavad Gita into Persian.
Akbar built a new capital, Fatehpur Sikri, near Agra
The entrance to Jamia Masjid, the Buland Darwaza, is the highest in India.
A king named Shah Jahan built the Agra Fort, Red Fort, Moti Mahal, Taj Mahal, and Mayura throne.
During the Mughal period, a new painting called Chikkini arose.
During Jahangir's time, painting was greatly encouraged.
During Akbar's time, he encouraged the art of music
The concert was divided into seven musical troupes, one a day.
Tansen was a famous musician of Akbar's court.

questions.text: What were the causes for the decline of the Mughal Empire?
questions.text_as_printed: What were the causes for the decline of the Mughal Empire? (Difficult)

answer.value:
The main reasons for the decline of the Mughal Empire were:
The empire was weakened by the corrupt rule of Aurangzeb
The Mughal sardars began to become corrupt.
There were fierce infighting for the succession to the throne.
The provincial authorities took advantage of this and ruled independently.
Most importantly, Aurangzeb's policy of transforming India into a Muslim state.
There was opposition everywhere.
Protracted conflicts with Sikhs, Rajputs and Marathas weakened the empire
They were completely emptied.
A Persian invader named Nadir Shah invaded Delhi.
He plundered the wealth that the Mughals had accumulated for two hundred years, and
He took away the world famous Kohinoor diamond and mayura throne.
The Mughal treasury was emptied and the Mughal Empire declined.
